newsitem.title: FRANCE: France wants to promote grain exports to Morocco.
newsitem.headline: France wants to promote grain exports to Morocco.

text.p: French grain producers, eager to foil competition from other world suppliers, notably the U.S., are considering opening a Moroccan office to promote French grain exports, officials from producer association AGBP said.
Producers are especially anxious to develop tighter links with the new breed of private operators unleashed by the recent liberalisation of Morocco's cereal sector, they said.
Representatives from the AGPB and from national grain office ONIC were part of an official visit French farm minister Philippe Vasseur made to Morocco last week.
Contacts with potential buyers were established during the visit, they said.
Grain exporters, who dealt mainly with Morocco's national grain office before liberalisation, said it was crucial to develop ties with private buyers, particularly millers.
"Morocco is our number one market. The number one market is no longer controlled by the state, so we have to set up a marketing strategy," ONIC president Michel Marie told Reuters.
Exporters believe that special marketing efforts must be made because fierce competition from the U.S. is looming.
"The U.S. seems determined to do business with Morocco. There is no reason for us not to be there," said APGB director general Georges Malpel.
He said the French grain industry was mulling a promotion system similar to the one set up by the U.S. Wheat Association, but he did not provide further details.
Morocco bought 2.4 million tonnes of wheat on world markets in the past campaign, including some 800,000 tonnes of French wheat.
Latest statistics from the International Grains Council suggest Morocco's wheat imports may slow down to 1.3 million tonnes in 1996/97, due to a record crop.
French bankers agreed in early October to extend to June 30, 1997 from June 30, 1996 the deadline for the expiry of a Coface credit guarantee allowing Morocco to buy French wheat.
Some 300,000 tonnes of wheat have been left unused out of the initial line, which was for purchasing one million tonnes.
